summary:
This project proposes an interactive, browser-based educational simulation called Artemis Cadet — a game-style application in which young learners (ages 7–14) take command of a small crewed outpost on the Moon or Mars. Players act as junior mission commanders responsible for keeping their crew alive and their base operational across a series of mission days or rounds. The name reflects NASA's Artemis programme and the player's role as a cadet learning to command an outpost.
At each turn, the player allocates limited resources — solar power, oxygen, water, food, and radiation shielding — and responds to mission events such as solar storms, micrometeorite impacts, equipment faults, and dust storms. Every choice carries a consequence: neglect power and life support fails; ignore radiation and crew health declines. The simulation is grounded in authentic NASA science and uses real mission-planning values wherever possible.
The project's core goal is to transform abstract space-science concepts into lived, decision-based experiences. Rather than reading about how astronauts survive in space, students make the decisions that determine survival — building systems thinking, scientific literacy, and genuine appreciation for the engineering behind human spaceflight.
